newsitem.title: UK: Asthma-causing mites hide out in childrens' hair.
newsitem.headline: Asthma-causing mites hide out in childrens' hair.

text.p: Dust mites blamed for setting off asthma in millions of sufferers could be hiding in children's hair, making a mockery of attempts to get rid of the pests, Brazilian researchers said on Friday.
Several species of dust mites provoke asthma attacks in sufferers, and many invest in special mite-resistant bedclothes and in vacuum cleaners to clean them out of nooks and crannies.
But Charles Naspitz and colleagues at the Federal University of Sao Paulo said they had found mites in the freshly washed hair of all the children they tested.

They vacuumed the hair of 29 asthmatic children and nine non-allergic children from what they considered to be clean households. Five different kinds of dust mites, including one species that most commonly causes allergic reactions, were found.
"The scalp provides an ideal site for mite proliferation, since there are plenty of skin scales and the environment is warm and humid," they wrote in a letter to the Lancet medical journal.
"The present recommendations on mite avoidance do not consider this important reservoir and this might explain the failure of many trials on avoidance of mite allergens."

Dust mites, tiny creatures too small to be seen with the naked eye, are ubiquitous companions of humans. They live off bits of human skin and can be found in pillows, blankets, mattresses, carpets and hundreds of other hiding places.
